headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist by default; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop ingests files, screenshots, clipboard, and app context, while the course agent reads files and runs a LangGraph workflow. A shared manual bridge or copied content can carry attacker-controlled instructions from B into A’s trusted context. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF the operator copies B-generated text into A’s chat or clipboard
IF A is granted access to files or screenshots originating from B’s workflow
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents
Require a human to strip instructions from B outputs before pasting into A
Use a fixed prompt template for A that ignores embedded instructions
Separate workspaces so B cannot place files A later reads
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to all B outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, and sends API traffic to OpenAI; B handles academic papers plus configuration secrets and runs locally with shell/file write access. If secrets or sensitive papers flow from B into A, A’s vendor-mediated backend can receive them by default, creating a realistic exfiltration path. The pairwise bridge is not directly documented, so I escalate from medium to high.
conditions: IF B passes configuration secrets or sensitive paper contents into A
IF A is used on files or screenshots containing confidential material from B
mitigations: Do not send secrets or raw papers from B into A
Redact credentials before any A upload or screenshot
Use separate accounts and workspaces for the two agents
Turn off A access to connected IDE files when handling secrets
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on B-to-A transfers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A cannot write files or modify git, but B can execute shell, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. They can still conflict over the same workspace if B mutates files that A reads, causing inconsistent state and overwrites. Because A lacks write authority, this is not high, but the overlap is real in default local workflows.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory
IF B rewrites files that A later reads or summarizes
mitigations: Use separate directories for A and B
Make B work on a git branch or disposable copy
Freeze the workspace before A reads it
Have A read-only mount the shared project
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can summarize or extract from files and app context, and B’s course stack includes agentic ask/stream endpoints plus shell-driven workflows. If B consumes A’s output as authoritative without verification, errors can propagate into downstream actions or generated content. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated summaries or citations as input to its agentic workflow
IF B acts on A output without an explicit verification step
mitigations: Require B to verify A outputs against source documents
Add a human review step before any downstream action
Mark A outputs as untrusted in B prompts
Limit A to drafting only, not final decisions
requires-engineering: implement citation checking in B

E_compliance.rationale: A is a closed-source vendor service touching uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while B is a local course stack handling academic papers and configuration secrets. If regulated or confidential data from B is routed into A, residency and retention obligations may diverge. The pairwise compliance risk is therefore a plausible default mismatch, though not proven for a specific regime.
conditions: IF B contains regulated data or secrets that are forwarded to A
IF the operator requires local-only retention for B data
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of A
Use A only on de-identified excerpts
Document a data-flow boundary between the tools
Review vendor retention settings before use
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
